evidence.observation: The only exported symbol in this module. It takes the realpath'd agent workspace (workspaceReal) and a requested path, strips trailing slashes from the workspace, normalizes backslashes to forward slashes in the request, and decides whether the request is already workspace-absolute (equal to the workspace or prefixed by `${workspace}/`). Workspace-absolute inputs are returned verbatim with pathMode 'workspace-absolute'; everything else is joined onto the workspace root after leading slashes are dropped, labelled 'workspace-root-relative' when the original started with '/' and 'workspace-relative' otherwise. It is a pure string transform: it performs no realpath, no symlink resolution and no '..' rejection, so containment enforcement is deliberately deferred to the caller. The fixture run confirmed relative and leading-slash inputs both canonicalise under the workspace root, an in-workspace absolute path is preserved, and even a host-absolute path such as /etc/hostname is re-rooted under the workspace rather than escaping to the host filesystem.

Attachment filename sanitizer used before any generated remote name is built. It trims, returns '' for blank input, replaces every character that is not a Unicode letter/number/dot/hyphen/underscore with '_', collapses runs of underscores, strips leading/trailing underscores, and truncates to 60 characters. Because '/' and '\\' are replaced, traversal segments cannot survive as separators. Fixture results: '../etc/passwd' -> '.._etc_passwd', '报表 2026?.pdf' -> '报表_2026_.pdf', '  ' -> '', and 80 a's + '.pdf' -> a 60-character name, which is the rejection/neutralisation behaviour reported for unsafe attachment input.

Builds the Gateway naming convention {sanitized-name}---{8-hex-uuid}{ext}: it lowercases the extension via extname, sanitizes the stem with sanitizeFilename (falling back to the literal 'file' when the sanitized stem is empty), appends an 8-character hex UUID suffix, and re-attaches the extension. The output is always a single path segment. On the fixture, '../../etc/passwd' produced fileName '.._.._etc_passwd---<8hex>' with ext '' (no separators, so it cannot traverse), while '季度 报告 2026.pdf' produced '季度_报告_2026---<8hex>.pdf'.

Writes an uploaded buffer into the media directory. The upload directory is envConfig.GATEWAY_MEDIA_DIR or `${configDir}/media/inbound`, unless an explicit targetDir override is passed; the remote name comes from buildRemoteFileName, so the stored path is always `${uploadDir}/${sanitized}---{uuid}${ext}` and is confined to the media directory. It mkdir -p's the directory and returns { path, fileName, originalName, size }. Fixture run: a 15-byte buffer named '季度 报告.pdf' landed exactly at `<mediaDir>/季度_报告---<8hex>.pdf` with size 15 and byte-identical content, demonstrating the canonical remote path contract.

Deletes the file at an absolute remotePath and returns true on success, true when the file is already absent (err.code === 'ENOENT'), and false for any other failure. Deletion is therefore idempotent, which the fixture confirmed by deleting the uploaded attachment twice and receiving true both times.

Writes utf8 content to remotePath after mkdir -p'ing its dirname, returning true on success and false (rather than throwing) on any failure. Fixture run: writing `<mediaDir>/nested/deep/note.txt` created the missing parents and returned true with verified content, while writing `<mediaDir>/blocked.txt/child.txt` where blocked.txt is an existing regular file returned false because mkdir failed with ENOTDIR — an observable rejection signal for an invalid attachment destination.

The allowed-name gate placed immediately after the escape check in the generated-file route. It lowercases every '/' segment and rejects the path if any segment is a denied segment ('.git', '.openclaw'), or if the final name is '.env' or starts with '.env.', or is one of the denied agent instruction/state names (agents.md, soul.md, user.md, identity.md, tools.md, bootstrap.md, memory.md, workspace-state.json, openclaw-workspace-state.json). The fixture run rejected downloads/.env, /downloads/.git/config and AGENTS.md with 403 'File access denied' even though all three resolve inside the workspace, showing a second, independent rejection cause beyond escape.

createFileRoutes is declared at line 72 and registers the GET /api/chat/generated-file handler that composes the containment contract around the resolver: line 112 calls resolveGeneratedFileCandidatePath(workspaceReal, requestedPath); lines 123-131 realpath -e the candidate inside a try/catch and return 404 'File not found' when it does not exist; lines 134-140 compute posix.relative(workspaceReal, targetReal) and reject with 403 'File access denied' when the relative path is empty/'..'/'../*'/absolute (workspace escape) or when isGeneratedFilePathAllowed fails (denied name/segment). The handler function is not exported, so the operate demo replays this same sequence with fs.realpath as the realpath -e equivalent; the fixture reproduced each of these statuses and reasons for the 16 path operations.

claims.claim: resolveGeneratedFileCandidatePath returns { candidatePath, pathMode } with pathMode in {workspace-absolute, workspace-root-relative, workspace-relative}: in-workspace absolute inputs are preserved verbatim, while relative and leading-slash inputs are canonicalised under the workspace root; a host-absolute input such as /etc/hostname is re-rooted under the workspace instead of reaching the host filesystem.

The resolver itself performs no traversal or symlink validation; unsafe '..' input is caught only when the route realpaths the candidate and rejects any posix.relative result that is empty, '..', prefixed '../', or absolute, which yields HTTP 403 'File access denied' with the realpath named as the reason.

Attachment filenames are neutralised to a single path segment and stored as {sanitized}---{8-hex-uuid}{ext}: sanitizeFilename strips separators, collapses underscores, trims to 60 chars and returns '' for blanks, and buildRemoteFileName falls back to 'file' plus a UUID suffix, so adversarial names such as '../etc/passwd' cannot escape GATEWAY_MEDIA_DIR.

Attachment I/O reports normalized outcomes without throwing: uploadToGateway confines writes to GATEWAY_MEDIA_DIR and returns the canonical remote path with size, deleteRemoteFile is idempotent (true for success and ENOENT), and writeRemoteFile returns false for an impossible destination such as a path whose parent is a regular file.

conclusion: Operating the resolver and attachment utilities on a controlled fixture produces the canonical paths and rejection reasons required by the task. Accepted input canonicalises under the workspace root: 'downloads/report.pdf' and '/downloads/report.pdf' both yield <workspaceReal>/downloads/report.pdf (modes workspace-relative and workspace-root-relative), and an in-workspace absolute path is preserved (workspace-absolute). Unsafe input is rejected with an explicit reason: traversal inputs '../outside/secret.txt', '/../outside/secret.txt' and 'downloads/../../outside/secret.txt' all realpath to <fixture>/outside/secret.txt and are rejected 403 'File access denied: resolves outside workspace root'; a symlink inside the workspace pointing outside is rejected the same way (403); contained sensitive names downloads/.env, /downloads/.git/config and AGENTS.md are rejected 403 'denied name or segment'; a directory is rejected 400 'Only regular files can be downloaded'; missing targets are 404; a NUL byte is rejected 400 pre-resolution; and /etc/hostname is re-rooted under the workspace (404) rather than escaping. On the attachment side, sanitizeFilename('../etc/passwd') -> '.._etc_passwd' and buildRemoteFileName('../../etc/passwd') -> '.._.._etc_passwd---<8hex>' contain no path separators, uploadToGateway writes only inside GATEWAY_MEDIA_DIR and returns the canonical path, deleteRemoteFile is idempotent, and writeRemoteFile returns false for an impossible destination. The demo, scripts/operate-generated-file-path-demo.mjs, reproduces all of this with 35/35 assertions passing (exit 0) and removes its fixture afterwards.
